content:
Days after rolling out its username reservation system, WhatsApp is now beginning to enable the full functionality for some users. Here are the details.

WhatsApp begins activating reserved usernames

Last month, WhatsApp launched a username reservation system that allows users to claim a unique username ahead of the full feature going live.

Users can navigate to Settings > Account > Username to claim their username, and can choose whether to allow anyone who knows the username to contact them, or to require new contacts to also enter a four-digit PIN code in addition to the username.

If the chosen username is identical to an existing account on other Meta platforms (such as Facebook or Instagram), users may be required to prove that they have control of the corresponding account. This measure is designed to prevent the abuse of well-known usernames, as well as impersonation that could be exploited for scams.

That said, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now starting to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts.

Users included in the first phase of the rollout can now see a banner at the top of their chat list indicating that their username has been activated and can be shared with new contacts.

The report notes that the feature is being pushed simultaneously to beta testers and users on the stable version of WhatsApp, but emphasises that it currently appears to be limited to a very small number of users.

To check whether your account has been activated, look for a relevant banner at the top of the chat list, or go to the Username section in your profile settings. The field will indicate whether your username has been activated, or display a message such as "Username coming soon — you will be notified when it's ready."
